claim.pdf_says: Table 12 — Procedural statements, DELETE row. The 'Conditional phrase' cell prints TWO stacked lines: '[NOT] INVALID KEY' on the first line and '[NOT] ON EXCEPTION' on the second line. Explicit scope terminator: 'END-DELETE'.
claim.markdown_says: | DELETE | [NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] ON EXCEPTION | END-DELETE |
claim.why_it_matters:
The two stacked entries are independent alternative conditional phrases of the DELETE statement; run together on one line they read as a single compound phrase '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] ON EXCEPTION'. The very same table uses '
' to preserve the stacking for every other multi-valued cell (IF -> 'THEN
ELSE', READ -> '[NOT] AT END
[NOT] INVALID KEY', SEARCH -> 'WHEN
AT END'), so this row is inconsistent with its own table. Table 12 is the normative source for which statements have conditional phrases and explicit scope terminators.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the 300dpi render of spec_p563.png plus pixel metrology; every particular of the claim checks out and the standard refutations all fail. (1) The PDF glyphs. Cropped and upscaled the DELETE row. The 'Conditional phrase' cell unambiguously prints two lines, both flush to the same left edge with no continuation indent: line 1: '[NOT] INVALID KEY' line 2: '[NOT] ON EXCEPTION' Third column reads 'END-DELETE'. The claim quotes the PDF exactly. (2) The markdown quote is exact. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23561 reads '| DELETE | [NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] ON EXCEPTION | END-DELETE |' — the two entries joined by a plain space, with no separator. Verified identical in the freshly generated work unit page-563.md line 29. Neither source is misquoted. (3) Refutation attempt: 'it is only line wrapping.' REFUTED by measurement. Vertical table rules on the page sit at x=1012 and x=1607; the measured cell inset is 23-25px on every column (col1 text starts 23px after its rule, col3 24px), so the usable text width is ~1037..1583. Token extents in the DELETE cell: line 1 '[NOT]'=1037-1143, 'INVALID'=1162-1323, 'KEY'=1339-1414 (ends at x=1414); inter-word gap = 19px; line 2's leading '[NOT]' is 106px wide. A greedy text wrap would therefore have set '[NOT]' at 1433..1539, comfortably inside the 1583 right boundary — i.e. a genuine wrap would have broken as '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT]' / 'ON EXCEPTION'. It did not. The break falls after 'KEY' leaving ~169px of unused slack, which only a hard line break produces. This is a deliberate two-entry stack, not reflow. (4) Independent corroboration of the table's convention, from page 564 (rendered separately): the IF row stacks 'THEN' over 'ELSE' — two tokens totalling well under a quarter of the cell width, which could not possibly be a wrap. Stacking in Table 12 therefore denotes separate alternative entries, and the transcription's own convention for it is '
', applied correctly three times on that page (IF 'THEN
ELSE' line 23582, READ '[NOT] AT END
[NOT] INVALID KEY' line 23593, SEARCH 'WHEN
AT END' line 23600). The DELETE row on page 563 violates the convention the same table obeys everywhere else. (5) Meaning does change. With the separator lost, the cell reads as one compound phrase '[NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] ON EXCEPTION' rather than two independent alternatives, and it is the only row in Table 12 whose cell would then contain a phrase sequence that is not a legal single conditional phrase. Table 12 is the normative index of conditional phrases and scope terminators (referenced by 14.5.2 and by 8.x general-format rules), so this is a content defect in a normative table, not typography — though the severity is fairly rated cosmetic, since an attentive reader still recovers the two phrases from DELETE's own general format. Nothing is missing from the transcription; what is lost is a semantically load-bearing structural separator. That is a genuine discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description:
Accurate as filed. One amendment, for completeness rather than correction: the defect is a two-instance pattern, not a lone row. The identical failure occurs in the final continuation of Table 12 on page 565, where the PDF stacks '[NOT] INVALID KEY' over '[NOT] END-OF-PAGE' in the WRITE row (verified against a 300dpi render) but specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23625 emits '| WRITE | [NOT] INVALID KEY [NOT] END-OF-PAGE | END-WRITE |'. Table 12 has five multi-entry conditional-phrase cells in total; the three on page 564 (IF, READ, SEARCH) carry '
' correctly, and both cells that straddle the other two pages (DELETE on 563, WRITE on 565) lost it. The fix for page 563 is '| DELETE | [NOT] INVALID KEY
[NOT] ON EXCEPTION | END-DELETE |', and the sibling on page 565 should be repaired in the same change set.
